prospect.name: Angelo
prospect.aka: iPhone (speaker label is a device name)
prospect.occupation: Currently not working and receiving disability — 'I get disability, so I don't really have to work unless I need to' — but about to start as a correctional officer doing security at a jail, explicitly to bring in extra money. US Army veteran, three years out, previously stationed in Germany with NATO.
prospect.family_status: Married; his wife is very fit and trains with him — 'she looks good, so I have to look good too'. Five children in total: a six-year-old daughter and two sons who live in California (his own), plus stepchildren aged seven and eight. Also a hyperactive Doberman. Has an ex-wife; his eldest son was born in Bavaria and holds German citizenship.
prospect.training_background: US Army physical training background — daily high-intensity PT, running, plus his own weights work. Since leaving three years ago he switched to bodybuilding-style lifting and bulking. Has done muscle-ups and bodyweight work. Started kettlebells about a week and a half before the call after two weeks of watching Trevor's YouTube videos, and mimics the videos at the gym.
prospect.medical: Hip injury from a convoy accident during military service — 'my hip is not, like, an old man hip' — which prevents him squatting or training legs heavily and forced him onto light leg work. Receives disability, though the basis was never asked. Self-reports ADHD with brain fog he links to diet: 'I'll be sitting there, you can talk to me, and my mind would just blow off... if I eat bad, I'm going to be all foggy.' He connects with Trevor partly because Trevor has spoken about having ADHD too.

Like monthly, I can probably pay', and asked what was left over at month end. Never quoted an instalment option on the $6,000; went straight to a $200/month community tier instead.

objections.rep_response: Pushed for more — 'Do you think you can push that to 200 a month?' — and asked three separate times what he had set aside, being told each time that his savings are ring-fenced family emergency funds he will not touch.

notable.note: Three things. First, the prospect did not hear the price when it was given. The rep quoted $6,000 at 00:36:37, got 'Okay. Perfect.' and immediately started arranging where to send the payment link — and only two minutes later did the prospect say 'Man, $6,000, man. Good gracious', with the rep having to ask 'Did you not hear me correctly when I said it?' A false positive that nearly resulted in a link being sent to someone who had not registered the number. Second, the rep disclosed his own history at length — that he was overweight six months ago, became a Trevor client, could not afford one-on-one himself at the time, started with the cheap tier, and was then invited to join the team. Good rapport and honest, but it also tells the prospect the cheap tier is what the rep himself bought, which undercuts the premium. Third, this is a man on disability with five children who said twice that his savings are ring-fenced family emergency money, and he was asked a third time what he had set aside. Worth reading alongside the Rudolph call the previous day, where the rep asked three times for an immediate start after being told there was nothing available. Also: the rep called him 'Dominic' at 00:01:49 and 'Angel' twice, having opened the call by asking how to pronounce his name — the fourth call in this batch with a name error.

Attribution inverts constantly: at 00:01:49 the rep's opening question sits inside a prospect block; the whole stretch from 00:04:14 to 00:05:47 alternates wrongly; the pillar presentation between 00:28:53 and 00:30:05 splits single rep sentences across both labels; at 00:38:50-00:39:04 the prospect's question 'how'd you get a job with him?' is attributed to the rep; and 00:46:24-00:46:26 assigns the rep's check question to the prospect.
